transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah. Well, to be honest, my sister kind of pushed me to make the appointment, but I guess what really brings me in is that my body just feels completely out of my control right now. It's been this whole crazy shift, and I don't really understand it. 

Like, at first, a little while ago, I was just constantly moving. I'm a waiter, so I'm used to being on my feet a lot anyway, but this was totally different—I was pacing around my apartment all night, literally all night, just walking back and forth making all these incredibly detailed notes for this underground supper club I was planning to open. I couldn't stop my legs, I just had to keep pacing and pacing while I was mapping out the menus and the seating arrangements and everything. 

But then... lately, it's like the exact opposite has happened. I'm just so incredibly slowed down. It feels like I'm trying to move through wet concrete. My sister came over to check on me the other day because I wasn't answering her texts, and we were supposed to go out, and she said it literally takes me forever just to get my shoes on. Like, I was just sitting there on the edge of the bed holding my sneakers, and my hands just felt too heavy to even tie the laces. I don't know what's going on with my body, but going from pacing a hole in the floor every single night to barely being able to dress myself... it's just really frustrating, you know?

When you were pacing all night working on the supper club plans, were you also feeling sad, hopeless, or down at that same time—or did that low, slowed-down feeling only start after the pacing phase had ended?

No, no, they were totally separate. Like, completely different phases, you know? When I was doing the supper club stuff, I wasn't sad at all. I mean, honestly, I felt amazing. I felt like I was on top of the world, like I had this brilliant vision that nobody else could see yet. I was so energized, so dialed in. The pacing wasn't because I was anxious or upset, it was just because there was so much electricity in my body, like my brain was working so fast that my legs had to keep up. I was sketching out these five-course tasting menus—I remember I had this whole concept for a deconstructed heirloom tomato salad that was going to blow people's minds—and I was just so focused and driven. I didn't feel hopeless even for a second. If anything, I felt like I had more hope and purpose than I've ever had in my entire life. 

It was only later, after all that completely stopped, that the heavy, slow feeling started. It was like someone just unplugged me from the wall. The pacing stopped, the ideas stopped, the energy just vanished. And that's when I started feeling so low and so... stuck. Like with the shoes, you know? Just sitting there staring at my sneakers, feeling like tying them was climbing Mount Everest. So, yeah, it definitely wasn't at the same time. The high, fast part happened first, and then it just completely crashed into this awful, slow, heavy thing. It's like two totally different people, honestly.
Have you had any new medical diagnoses, started any new medications, or used any recreational drugs or alcohol around the time these energy and mood changes began?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't really go to the doctor much anyway, so definitely no new diagnoses. The last time I went to a doctor before this was probably... gosh, maybe three years ago? I had this really weird rash on my arm from carrying these massive, heavy trays at work—because the restaurant I work at, they use these huge ceramic plates that weigh a ton, and they expect you to balance like four of them on one arm. Anyway, it was just contact dermatitis or something, they gave me a cream. But lately? No, nothing medical. 

And no new medications either. I don't even like taking Tylenol unless I absolutely have to, you know? My mom was always really big on natural remedies when I was growing up, so I just kind of got used to toughing things out or drinking peppermint tea or whatever. So I'm definitely not on any prescriptions. 

As for drugs or alcohol... I mean, I'll have a beer after a really long shift sometimes, just to unwind because being a waiter is so physically exhausting. You're dealing with people's demands for eight hours straight, running back and forth from the kitchen to the floor, and sometimes you just need a drink to decompress. But I didn't drink at all during that whole supper club phase. I didn't want to. I didn't even have time to think about drinking because I was so consumed with the menus and the planning. Alcohol would have just slowed me down, and I needed to be sharp, you know? I needed my brain to be completely clear so I could get all those ideas out on paper. And I don't do any recreational drugs. Never have. I've always been kind of paranoid about that stuff, to be honest. I saw a guy at a party once have a really bad trip on something, and it just totally freaked me out. So, yeah, no drugs, no new meds, no medical stuff. It's just... this is all just happening on its own, completely out of nowhere.
